title: Korea's privacy commission recommends stronger personal-data protection at Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company
date_note: Etnews (26 Nov) says the commission reviewed the three companies at a plenary meeting on 25 November.
geo_basis: Personal Information Protection Commission, South Korea; Seoul city centre
summary: Etnews reports that South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission recommended stronger personal-data protection at Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company, three firms involved in mergers or acquisitions. It recommended that Asiana's personal data be destroyed without delay once its purpose is fulfilled after the merger, and tighter oversight of Gmarket's outsourced processors. The article gives no penalties.
plain: Etnews reports that Korea's privacy regulator recommended stronger data protection at Korean Air, Gmarket and Remember & Company after reviewing their mergers or acquisitions. The article mentions no penalties.
exec: Etnews reports that Korea's privacy regulator issued data-protection recommendations to three companies tied to mergers or acquisitions; no penalties are mentioned.
action: Etnews reports the commission's guidance: a chief privacy officer should be responsible for transfers, transfer only necessary data in encrypted form, and check afterwards whether any data was lost.

validation.note: Etnews only; it relays the commission's plenary decision of 25 November. The commission's own page was not found or read.

review.note: Compared companies, 25 Nov plenary, Asiana, Gmarket processors, guidance, no penalties against Etnews
